cim_eredeti: Will Artificial Intelligence Create Wealth in Portugal or Just Consume Energy?
szoveg_eredeti:
Portugal is attracting a new generation of investments associated with artificial intelligence and data centres.

By Paulo Lopes, in Business · 15 Nov 2026, 09:01 · 0 Comments

The geographical location, international connectivity and energy potential put the country in an interesting position, with technological operators looking for new infrastructure in Europe. The announcements of large-scale projects are naturally positive, but I believe that we should ask a more demanding question: how much of the wealth generated by this technological transformation will actually remain in the Portuguese economy?

Colliers' most recent study reveals that Lisbon has approximately 1,389 MW IT in data centre projects, despite currently having only 25 MW IT operational. In Sines, Start Campus has authorisation for a total capacity of 1.2 GW, accompanied by plans to install computing equipment for artificial intelligence. These investments can strengthen Portugal's international position, but they also represent significant needs for energy, infrastructure and execution capacity.

A data centre can mobilise high capital without necessarily creating an equivalent number of permanent jobs. A large part of the computer equipment can be imported, and the digital services processed on the premises can generate revenue for companies based in other countries. This does not mean that the projects are of little relevance. It only means that we must distinguish between announced investment, economic activity produced and value actually captured by the national economy. They are different realities, and all deserve to be evaluated.

Portugal should seek to maximise the benefits of these investments through the participation of national companies, the training of specialised professionals and the development of complementary technological activities. Portuguese universities, research centres and companies can find opportunities in engineering, maintenance, energy management and the development of artificial intelligence applications. It is also essential to ensure that the use of energy infrastructure is planned efficiently, without compromising the competitiveness of other economic activities or transferring unjustified costs to other consumers.

Artificial intelligence could become one of the engines of the world economy in the coming decades. Portugal has the opportunity to participate in this transformation, but it should not limit its ambition to the installation of equipment and the supply of electricity. We need to create knowledge, develop companies, attract talent and build economic activities capable of generating added value. Success should not be measured only by the megawatts installed or the millions invested. It should be measured by the wealth, skills and opportunities that remain in the country. Because hosting the infrastructure of the digital economy is important, but truly participating in that economy is much more relevant.
